howDoI.q: How do I make a boss that changes as it is hurt?
How do I make a boss that gets faster at half health?
How do I make a monster walk back and forth?
How do I make a monster that blocks a narrow way?
How do I give a boss a new look for its last hit?
How do I make a monster leave a puff when it is beaten?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Three Phases is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels about a boss that changes as it is hurt, and takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each idea is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. Enter throws a star the way you last walked. F2 shows your hit points, lives and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

The one idea

Game-Maker has no boss with phases. A monster does one thing: it walks its path and a star kills it. So a boss that changes is a chain of different monsters. When a star kills the first, it becomes the second, in the same place, and the second has its own picture and its own, faster path. That is a phase. The last one becomes a puff.

pages.head: Level 1: Half Way
pages.html:
Level 1: Half Way

The HALF WAY IT SPEEDS UP sign stands near the start. Big Bug paces a long, low tunnel through a brick wall and there is no room to get past it. Stand a few steps back at the mouth of the tunnel, wait for it to walk close and press Enter. A star that misses is gone, so throw again. Two hits and the green bug turns into a quicker orange one, which takes two more. Each hit scores 20 points.

The TOUCHING ONLY STINGS sign says what happens if you try to push past: it costs Kit a few hit points and counts for nothing. Eight coins are on the way to the door.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • Four monsters, not one. Open phase.mon in the monsters editor. Monsters 5 to 8 are the chain. Each has When destroyed it becomes set to the next one: 5 becomes 6, 6 becomes 7, 7 becomes 8. The count of monsters is the count of hits.
  • The two phases. Monsters 5 and 6 use the green bug pictures and walk slowly. Monsters 7 and 8 use the orange bug pictures and walk faster: look at their Movement paths. Each path goes a block or two left, then right and back, and the number on each corner is how fast it goes.
  • The last hit. Monster 8 becomes monster 14, the puff, which has a For a set time of 18 ticks and then goes away on its own.
  • Where it sits. The map has only the first one, monster 5, in the tunnel. The rest appear in its place as stars land. Open one.map in the map editor.
  • Stars win, touching loses. Every stage has Power 150. A star has 200, so it wins. A touch from Kit cannot kill anything with Power 100 or more, so only stars count.
  • It blocks the tunnel. Open phase.mbl in the blocks editor: the bug pictures are Solid on every side and take 1 hit point for each moment you touch them. The tunnel is two blocks high, the hero’s own height, with no way over or around.
  • The score. Each stage’s Score when destroyed by a weapon is 20.
  • The star. Kit’s Throw sequence gives birth to monster 3, with a For a set time long enough to cross the whole tunnel. See hero.chr on the characters tab: the same star as in the Throw It Starter.

pages.head: Level 2: A Third Face
pages.html:
Level 2: A Third Face

The THE LAST HIT IS A NEW FACE sign comes first. The bug has five stages this time: two calm, two hurried and, for the last hit, a tiny purple one with a pink bow that is quickest of all. The THROW WHEN IT COMES CLOSE sign says how to aim: the tiny one is fast, so wait for it to turn toward you. Seven coins lie along the way.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • Five monsters. In the monsters editor, monsters 9 to 13 are a second chain. 9 and 10 are the calm green bug, 11 and 12 the hurried orange one, and 13 is a third monster with a third picture: the tiny purple bug, with the quickest path.
  • A new picture is a new monster. There is nothing to switch on. Open phase.mbl in the blocks editor: calm0, hurry0 and tiny0 are three drawings, each with a second wiggle frame. Each monster shows its own.
  • The last link. Monster 12 becomes monster 13 and monster 13 becomes the puff, monster 14.
  • The map. Open two.map. Only monster 9 is placed, in the tunnel.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

These are the engine’s limits, so you can plan around them.

  • No hit points to read. A monster has no number that goes down, so nothing can see how many hits are left or switch phase at “half”. The phase is just which monster in the chain is alive.
  • A phase starts where the last one fell. The next monster takes over in the same spot and starts its path from there. A boss that walks drifts a little from hit to hit, so this one paces a few blocks either side of where it stands, inside a long tunnel.
  • Every phase dies to the same thing. A star kills any of them. A phase that needs a different kind of shot needs the Showcase Tricks.
  • Hits cannot be undone. A bug does not heal. Leave the level and come back and it starts again from the first.
  • One hit a star. A star is used up by what it hits, so a boss never takes two hits from one throw.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • In phase.mon, give monster 6 the orange pictures too: the bug turns hurried after one hit instead of two.
  • Change a monster’s Movement speeds and watch the bug in the tunnel.
  • Swap the pictures of monsters 11 and 13, and the tiny one comes before the orange one.
  • Untick Solid on a bug picture and walk through it.
  • Make the star’s Power lower than 150 and see that a star no longer hurts it.

The home page’s Starters tab has more small games like this one.
